Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) requires choosing a **soft-thresholding power β** such that the scale-free topology fit index reaches a plateau \[1\]. The canonical figure is a two-panel plot: (left) the scale-free fit index vs β and (right) the mean connectivity vs β — the layout standardized by the FigureYa collection \[2\]. This tutorial simulates expression data and walks through the fitting step.

## Example

![](../images/Correlation/WgcnaPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="WgcnaPlot DEMO" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming Language: R

-   Dependent packages: `ggplot2`; `dplyr`; `patchwork`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggplot2")
if (!requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("dplyr")
if (!requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("patchwork")

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

With real data, you would use `WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold()` on the expression matrix. We simulate the scale-free topology fit index and mean connectivity for a range of β values, mimicking the output structure.

```{r load data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(2201)
powers <- c(1:10, seq(12, 20, by = 2))
fit_index <- 1 - exp(-0.3 * powers) + rnorm(length(powers), sd = 0.02)
mean_conn <- exp(-0.8 * powers) * 100 + rnorm(length(powers), sd = 1)

sft <- data.frame(power = powers, fit_index = fit_index, mean_conn = mean_conn)
head(sft)
```

## Visualization

### 1. Scale-Free Topology Fit and Mean Connectivity

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1SoftThreshold
#| fig-cap: "Scale-free topology fit index (left) and mean connectivity (right) vs soft-thresholding power β. The dashed line marks fit index = 0.8."
#| out.width: "95%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5

p1 <- ggplot(sft, aes(power, fit_index)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#B2182B", size = 2.5) +
  geom_line(colour = "#B2182B", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_text(aes(label = power), vjust = -0.8, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Soft-thresholding power (β)", y = "Scale-free topology fit index") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p2 <- ggplot(sft, aes(power, mean_conn)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#445EAD", size = 2.5) +
  geom_line(colour = "#445EAD", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = power), vjust = -0.8, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Soft-thresholding power (β)", y = "Mean connectivity") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

library(patchwork)
p1 + p2 + patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   Choose the lowest β where the fit index reaches ≥ 0.8 (the dashed line) — a higher β reduces connectivity but may lose biological signal.
-   With real data, use `WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold(expr_data, powerVector = powers, networkType = "unsigned")`.
-   If no β reaches 0.8, the data may not follow a scale-free topology; check for batch effects or use a different network type.
:::

## Application

WGCNA soft-threshold fitting is the first step in co-expression network analysis; the chosen β determines the adjacency matrix used for module detection.

## Reference

\[1\] Langfelder P, Horvath S. WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics. 2008;9:559. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-559

\[2\] Xiaofan Lu, et al. FigureYa: A Standardized Visualization Framework for Enhancing Biomedical Data Interpretation and Research Efficiency. iMetaMed. 2025. doi:10.1002/imm3.70005
